access.add_first: Who is coming in, and as what. The first person has to be able to admin: a console with people on it and nobody who may admin refuses to start.
access.add_who: The name your gateway reports (e.g. lee@corp.com)
access.exceptions_why: Somebody given something their group does not give them.
access.groups_why: Maintained where people are hired and let go. This console only says what membership means here.
access.instance_why: This list governs this magi only. Another account, or another machine, keeps its own.
access.lead: Everybody who reaches this console is checked against this list. What a group and a person both allow ADDS UP — two matches mean both, never less.
access.nobody: Nobody is listed yet: this console runs as one operator, with no policy.
access.nobody_how: Adding the first person turns the gate on for everybody.
access.nobody_unnamed: Nobody can be added until this console is started with -user-header, behind a gateway that sets it: naming the first person turns the gate on, and a console that cannot tell who anybody is would then refuse everybody.
access.remove_body: They will no longer see anything on this console. You can add them back at any time.
access.who: Their name, as the gateway reports it
access.why: Who may use this console, and how much
answer.instead: Answering the question above; to ask for something else, answer it or interrupt first
answer.or_pick: Pick one above, or write a different answer here
ask.question: a question
board.nothing_how: Pick another day, or today, to see what each companion was working on.
cap.admin: People, roles, and admitting other machines — the one that can grant the others.
cap.answer: Answer what a companion is blocked on, and stop a turn. Not the same as deciding what it works on.
cap.configure: Change how it runs: the model, the approval mode, the schedule, the tool servers.
cap.curate: Change what a companion learns from: the experience store and the shape of its reports.
cap.prompt: Give a companion work: send, steer, dispatch, compact, move it to another conversation.
cap.read: See the companions, their transcripts, history and search. Looks, changes nothing.
cap.shell: Run a command in the workspace, outside the approval policy a tool call goes through.
copy.refused: the browser would not let this page copy
detail.evidence_decide: What it is asking you to decide on
detail.evidence_gone: summarised away — this round's material is no longer in the log
detail.judged_on_report: none observed — judged on the report's substance
detail.keep: Keep — the revision must not lose this
detail.no_changes: No files changed — a read-only turn.
embed.none: No embedding model, so searches match on wording only
empty.no_agents: No magi is running under this config directory
empty.no_agents_how: Start one with magi --daemon in a workspace
empty.no_match_how: Try fewer words, or a word the note itself would use
empty.no_servers_how: A companion can read and run things here; an MCP server is how it reaches anything else.
empty.nothing_learned_how: A companion writes one here when it decides something is worth keeping. You can write one yourself, below — a rule you have had to give three of them is a rule.
field.report_format: What it brings you when it asks
files.delete_body: The file goes. If git is tracking it, git can put it back; if it is not, nothing can. The companion is told either way — its context still holds a file that is no longer there.
files.elsewhere: Only gossip reaches this companion, so its files stay on its own machine. A magi-web running there, added here as a peer, opens them like any other.
files.look: Let the model read the file I am editing
files.look_why: In the file editor only, and while you are typing: on a pause it says what looks wrong in the buffer — a bug, a typo in a name, a case not handled — and says nothing when there is nothing to say. It spends the companion’s model on every pause, and it never saves or sends anything.
files.unreadable: This companion did not answer for its workspace.
fmt.about: The agent must fill every section here before it may put a decision to you. A missing one is refused, and the question does not reach you until it is filled.
fmt.headline: What it must bring when it asks
git.commit_who: What changed, and why. The subject line is the one that gets read.
git.discard_body: The file goes back to the last commit. This is the one thing here that cannot be undone by pressing the other button — and the companion is told, because its context still holds what is about to be gone.
git.group_changed: Changed — a commit would leave these
git.group_staged: Staged — a commit would take these
git.not_a_repo: This workspace is not a git checkout — nothing here is under version control.
git.pr_who: The branch is pushed first. The first line is the title; everything under it is the body.
git.stash_body: Everything uncommitted goes into a stash, untracked files included, and the tree goes back to the last commit. "Restore stash" brings it back.
git.switch_body: Every file in it may be a different version afterwards, and the companion is told so — its context still holds what is here now.
git.unreachable: This companion did not answer about its git state. It may have stopped.
hint.compact: Summarise the older turns. The detail stays on disk and can be recalled, but the live window loses the original wording
hint.edit_server: Changes {file}. It attaches when that daemon next starts
hint.forget: Remove this rule from the store
hint.mcp_args: One per line, or separated by spaces
hint.mcp_command: For example npx. Leave empty for an HTTP server
hint.mcp_env: NAME=value, written to the config file
hint.mcp_url: For an HTTP server, scheme and all
hint.session_busy: It is working — a session cannot be left mid-turn
hint.session_pick: Open another of this workspace's sessions
insp.tools_unknown: This companion did not say. A daemon started before this console knew to ask cannot answer — it is not that there are no tools.
map.lead: Where the fleet is running, and what is crossing between its parts. A box is one magi — one account on one machine, with its own config directory, policy and key.
may.not_answer: You may not answer for this companion
may.not_prompt: You may not give this companion work
may.nothing: This console does not know you
may.nothing_how: Ask an operator to give you a role. Until then there is nothing here to show you.
meet.collecting: Asking each of them what they will do
meet.done_spent: Finished — it ran out of rounds rather than out of things to say
meet.ends: It ends when nobody has anything left to add — the participants decide that, not a number. You can wrap it up at any point, and this console stops a room that will not.
meet.finished: Finished, with something to hand out
meet.getting: Getting ready — {n} of {of} have read their workspace
meet.gone_how: A meeting lives in the console that convened it, and ends when that console does.
meet.leave_why: The meeting carries on without you — this console is what drives it
meet.need_two: Pick at least two companions — with one it is a conversation, and its own page does that better.
meet.reopen_needs_why: Say what they still have to answer — reopening without it asks nothing
meet.reopen_why: What they still have to answer
meet.resting: passed twice — name them to bring them back
meet.tasks: What each of them will do
meet.title: Meeting
meet.why: Ask several companions one question. They read each other's answers in turn, and each leaves with something to do — or with nothing, which is an ordinary outcome.
meet.yours: Waiting for you — say it, or leave the box empty to give the floor back
move.body: This companion is in {from}. Sending here moves it to {to} first, and the reply arrives there.
move.busy_why: A companion cannot leave a conversation it is still working in. Interrupt it, or wait.
move.headline: Continue {to} instead?
nav.companions_sub: Who is here, and on what
nav.meet_sub: Ask several of them at once
notify.demo: This is the demo. A running console can notify you; this copy has nothing watching a fleet.
notify.denied: This browser was told no. Only its own settings can undo that.
notify.how: This browser will be told when a companion starts waiting, even with the page closed.
notify.insecure: Only over https or localhost. An ssh tunnel to localhost counts.
notify.is_on: This browser is subscribed. Add the page to a home screen to be woken there too.
notify.nokey: This console has no push key
notify.unsupported: This browser has no push support
perm.allow: ask only when a guardrail insists
perm.ask: ask before it writes, runs or reaches out
perm.auto: edits go through; commands and network ask
perm.deny: refuse writing, running and reaching out
side.nothing: Nothing to show about this one yet
stop.body: The turn stops where it is. What it has already written stays, and you can say something new.
stop.headline: Interrupt {name}?
